Question 24(b) [3 marks]: How could a business improve management of its accounts receivable turnover?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 3):
3 marks: Shows how a business could improve the management of its accounts receivable turnover
2 marks: Sketches in general terms how a business's accounts receivable turnover could be improved
1 marks: Makes a general statement about accounts receivable turnover or working capital management

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
The accounts receivable turnover measures how long it takes the business to collect money from its debtors. The business wants to improve its cash flow by decreasing the length of time it takes to collect its debts thus reducing financial costs. This could be done by using debt collection agencies or factoring. These however are a cost to the business. The business offering a shorter interest-free period will also improve its accounts receivable turnover.



WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: demonstrate what liquidity is and why it is an objective of financial management (a)
Better responses: demonstrate the ways a relevant strategy could improve the management of the accounts receivable turnover (b)
Better responses: provide clear and detailed advantages and disadvantages of using both leasing and mortgages (c).
To improve: providing reasons why liquidity is an objective – not just defining what liquidity is (a)
To improve: focusing on the ways a business could improve the accounts receivable turnover rather than providing characteristics and features of a strategy (b)
To improve: providing more than just a description of leasing and mortgages (c).
